system.name: Omega Centauri
system.description: The largest and most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way, 17,000 light-years away in Centaurus. It contains roughly 10 million stars spanning 150 light-years, and may be the stripped nucleus of a dwarf galaxy absorbed long ago. It is thought to harbour an intermediate-mass black hole at its centre.

omegacentauri.name: Omega Centauri
omegacentauri.description: A globular cluster of roughly 10 million stars, visible to the naked eye as a blurry star in the southern sky. Unlike most globular clusters it contains multiple stellar populations of different ages and metallicities, strongly suggesting it is the remnant core of a dwarf galaxy stripped by the Milky Way's gravity over billions of years.
omegacentauri.funFact: Omega Centauri may harbour an intermediate-mass black hole of ~40,000 solar masses at its centre — a class of black holes so rare that this would be only the second ever confirmed, bridging the gap between stellar and supermassive black holes.
